hero.title: Chandragupta Maurya: The First Unifier
hero.description: Founder of the Mauryan Empire who consolidated vast territories and established a centralized imperial administration.

cards.details: Overthrow of the Nanda Dynasty and ascension to the throne of Magadha.
Conflict with Seleucus I Nicator and subsequent treaty involving land cessions.
Abdication of the throne and death via Sallekhana at Shravanabelagola.

items.title: M.A.I.N
items.decryption: Mudrarakshasa (Vishakhadatta), Arthashastra (Kautilya), Indica (Megasthenes), and Greek accounts provide the primary narrative for his reign.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Do not confuse Chandragupta Maurya with Chandragupta I of the Gupta Dynasty (a common chronological error).
Megasthenes did not visit India during Ashoka's time; he was the ambassador in Chandragupta's court.
Arthashastra is not a book on economics alone, but a treatise on Statecraft, Politics, and Administration.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Centered in Pataliputra (Magadha).
  • Expanded into Indus valley, Kabul, Herat, and Kandahar.

Personalities

  • Kautilya (Chanakya): Political mentor.
  • Megasthenes: Greek Ambassador.
  • Seleucus Nicator: Greek adversary turned ally.
  • Rise to Power: Overthrew Dhana Nanda (Nanda Dynasty) with Chanakya's strategic help.
  • Administration: Centralized autocracy described by Megasthenes (7-caste system) and Kautilya's Saptanga Theory.
  • Military: Massive standing army including infantry, cavalry, chariots, and elephants.
FeatureMauryan Policy
EconomyLand revenue as main source; State control over mines.
SocialRigid hierarchy; Slavery mentioned by Megasthenes but debated.

practiceQuestions.q: Who is traditionally credited with the foundation of the Mauryan Empire in ancient India?
practiceQuestions.sol: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire in 321 BCE by overthrowing the Nanda dynasty with the guidance of Chanakya (Kautilya).

practiceQuestions.q: Which Greek general and ruler of the Seleucid Empire was defeated by Chandragupta Maurya around 305 BCE?
practiceQuestions.sol: Chandragupta Maurya defeated Seleucus Nicator, leading to a treaty where Seleucus ceded vast territories and offered a matrimonial alliance.

practiceQuestions.q: Name the Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus Nicator to the court of Chandragupta Maurya at Pataliputra.
practiceQuestions.sol: Megasthenes was the Greek ambassador sent to Pataliputra, and his account 'Indica' provides valuable insights into Mauryan administration and society.

practiceQuestions.q: According to Jain tradition, which Jain monk accompanied Chandragupta Maurya to Shravanabelagola in his final days?
practiceQuestions.sol: In his later years, Chandragupta abdicated the throne, converted to Jainism under the guidance of Bhadrabahu, and migrated to Shravanabelagola.

practiceQuestions.q: By what name is Chandragupta Maurya referred to in Greek and Latin accounts (written by writers like Justin and Strabo)?
practiceQuestions.sol: Greek scholars identified Sandrokottos or Androkottos as Chandragupta Maurya, a key historical link established by Sir William Jones.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the name of the ritual fasting unto death practiced by Chandragupta Maurya at Shravanabelagola?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sallekhana (or Santhara) is the Jain religious ritual of voluntary fasting to death, which Chandragupta Maurya performed.

practiceQuestions.q: Which ancient political treatise, traditionally attributed to Kautilya (Chanakya), served as the administrative guide for Chandragupta Maurya?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Arthashastra provides comprehensive insights into statecraft, economic policy, military strategy, and legal systems under Chandragupta.

practiceQuestions.q: Who wrote the Sanskrit drama 'Mudrarakshasa', which details how Chanakya maneuvered Chandragupta to the throne and thwarted plots?
practiceQuestions.sol: Vishakhadatta authored 'Mudrarakshasa', a political drama that elaborates on the rise of Chandragupta and the diplomatic brilliance of Chanakya.

practiceQuestions.q: In which state of modern India is Shravanabelagola located, where Chandragupta Maurya spent his final days?
practiceQuestions.sol: Shravanabelagola is located in the Hassan district of Karnataka and is a prominent Jain pilgrimage center.

practiceQuestions.q: According to Greek sources, what was the approximate size of the standing army maintained by Chandragupta Maurya?
practiceQuestions.sol: Pliny and other classical writers note that Chandragupta maintained a massive professional army consisting of 600,000 infantry, 30,000 cavalry, and 9,000 elephants.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the geopolitical landscape of northwestern India change as a direct outcome of Chandragupta Maurya's conflict with Seleucus Nicator?
opts: India became a vassal state of the Seleucid Empire.
Chandragupta acquired vast territories including Aria, Arachosia, Gedrosia, and Paropamisadae in exchange for war elephants.
The Greek rulers permanently annexed the Indus Valley region.
It resulted in a total economic blockade of Pataliputra by Greek fleets.
practiceQuestions.sol: The treaty of 303 BCE resulted in Seleucus ceding the satrapies of Kabul, Kandahar, Herat, and Baluchistan (modern Afghanistan/Pakistan regions) to Chandragupta in exchange for 500 war elephants, effectively unifying northern and northwestern India under one imperial umbrella.

practiceQuestions.q: In the administrative structure described by Megasthenes and Kautilya, how was the municipal administration of Pataliputra organized?
opts: By a single hereditary mayor appointed directly by the king.
By a municipal board of thirty members divided into six committees of five members each.
By a democratic assembly elected by all adult male citizens.
By military generals who handled both law enforcement and revenue collection without civilian oversight.
practiceQuestions.sol: Megasthenes details that Pataliputra's city administration was run by a commission of 30 members divided into 6 specialized boards looking after industrial arts, foreigners, birth/death registration, trade/commerce, supervision of manufactured goods, and tax collection.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is Chandragupta Maurya historically designated as the 'First Unifier' of India?
opts: He was the first to enforce a single uniform religious code across the entire Indian subcontinent.
He successfully integrated fragmented regional states from the Gangetic plains to the frontiers of Iran and parts of the Deccan under a centralized bureaucratic apparatus.
He eliminated all regional languages and established Sanskrit as the sole spoken language.
He united all republican confederacies into autonomous democratic republics.
practiceQuestions.sol: Chandragupta Maurya is termed the first unifier because his conquests brought disparate mahajanapadas, kingdoms, and northwestern borderlands under a unified, centralized imperial framework for the first time in Indian history.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the economic and revenue administration under Chandragupta Maurya ensure stability across his vast empire?
opts: By relying solely on voluntary donations and religious tithes.
By instituting state-controlled agriculture, monopolies on mining and salt, and a systematic agrarian taxation system overseen by an officer called Samaharta.
By abolishing all taxes to encourage private merchant capitalism.
By outsourcing tax collection entirely to foreign mercenaries.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Arthashastra details a rigorous fiscal framework where the Samaharta (collector-general) managed revenue from crown lands, forests, mines, and trade, providing the financial backbone for a massive standing army and administrative machinery.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of the espionage network ('Gudhapurushas') established during Chandragupta's reign?
opts: They functioned purely as cultural ambassadors to foreign Hellenistic courts.
They served as a comprehensive intelligence apparatus keeping tabs on ministers, officials, citizens, and potential rebellions across the centralized empire.
They were solely responsible for managing the royal treasury and minting punch-marked coins.
They acted as religious priests who conducted state sacrifices.
practiceQuestions.sol: Kautilya's Arthashastra elaborates on a sophisticated spy network ('Gudhapurushas') comprising stationary and wandering agents, which was essential for maintaining internal security and bureaucratic oversight in a newly unified empire.

practiceQuestions.q: How did Chandragupta Maurya's military strategy differ from the preceding regional kingdoms?
opts: He relied solely on guerrilla warfare in mountainous terrains.
He institutionalized a permanent, centrally paid standing army equipped with specialized arms boards, replacing ad-hoc tribal militias.
He completely abandoned the use of war elephants in favor of naval fleets.
He depended entirely on Greek mercenaries for all military campaigns.
practiceQuestions.sol: Unlike earlier periods where kings relied on temporary levies or tribal fighters during times of war, Chandragupta and Chanakya established a full-time professional standing army with distinct departments for infantry, cavalry, chariots, elephants, navy, and transport.

practiceQuestions.q: What role did Chanakya play in the consolidation of Chandragupta's political authority?
opts: He acted as a spiritual guru who encouraged Chandragupta to renounce worldly power.
He served as the mastermind strategist, prime minister, and chief architect of Mauryan statecraft, governance, and diplomacy.
He was a foreign mercenary leader who commanded the northern cavalry.
He focused exclusively on foreign trade agreements with Roman merchants.
practiceQuestions.sol: Chanakya (Kautilya) was the chief political mentor and prime minister whose tactical brilliance, administrative blueprints (Arthashastra), and ruthless diplomacy enabled Chandragupta to defeat the Nandas and unify the empire.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the Mauryan administrative apparatus under Chandragupta handle regional diversity and distant provinces?
opts: By enforcing identical laws and customs across every single village without exception.
By dividing the empire into provinces (like Takshasila and Ujjain) governed by royal princes (Kumaras) while maintaining a central bureaucratic oversight.
By granting absolute independence to all regional governors without any central interference.
By replacing all local populations with settlers from Pataliputra.
practiceQuestions.sol: The empire was decentralized at the provincial level for efficient governance. Major provinces were overseen by royal princes or governors, balancing centralized imperial control with regional administrative adaptability.

practiceQuestions.q: What does the transition of Chandragupta Maurya from a military conqueror to a Jain ascetic signify in terms of ancient Indian political culture?
opts: The total collapse of the Mauryan administrative machinery immediately upon his retirement.
The coexistence of robust statecraft and personal spiritual pursuits, reflecting the fluid religious environment and the prevalence of ascetic traditions in ancient India.
That Mauryan emperors were prohibited by law from holding power for more than ten years.
The adoption of Buddhism as the mandatory state religion across all conquered provinces.
practiceQuestions.sol: Chandragupta's voluntary abdication of the throne to embrace Jain monkhood highlights how political rulers in ancient India frequently patronized or adhered to ascetic philosophies later in life, demonstrating a distinct philosophical dimension to Indian kingship.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the trade and commerce policies under Chandragupta Maurya reflect state intervention as outlined in the Arthashastra?
opts: The state maintained absolute laissez-faire with zero taxes or regulations on merchants.
The state actively regulated markets, standardized weights and measures, appointed superintendents (Panyadhyaksha) to monitor trade, and monopolized critical commodities.
Foreign trade was strictly banned, and all commercial transactions had to be conducted via barter only.
Merchants were permitted to mint their own independent coinage without state supervision.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Arthashastra illustrates a highly regulated mercantile economy where the state controlled prices, checked adulteration, penalized hoarding, and oversaw internal and external trade through specialized state officials.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Chandragupta Maurya:
1. He established the Mauryan Empire after defeating the last Nanda ruler, Dhana Nanda, with the assistance of Chanakya.
2. His empire's territorial boundaries extended into parts of modern-day Afghanistan and Baluchistan following his treaty with Seleucus Nicator.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Chandragupta overthrew Dhana Nanda in 321 BCE with Chanakya's counsel. After defeating Seleucus Nicator in 305 BCE, the resulting treaty in 303 BCE gave Chandragupta vast territories in the northwest, including areas in modern Afghanistan and Pakistan.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about sources detailing Chandragupta Maurya:
1. 'Indica', written by the Greek ambassador Megasthenes, provides firsthand accounts of Pataliputra's administration and Mauryan society.
2. The Sanskrit drama 'Mudrarakshasa' by Vishakhadatta sheds light on Chanakya's diplomatic manoeuvres and Chandragupta's accession to power.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are accurate. Megasthenes' 'Indica' (though surviving only in fragments) and Vishakhadatta's 'Mudrarakshasa' are vital literary pillars for understanding Chandragupta's reign and statecraft.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the administration of justice under Chandragupta Maurya:
1. The Arthashastra outlines a dual court system consisting of Dharmasthiya (civil courts) and Kantakasodhana (criminal/police courts).
2. Punishments for crimes during this period were extremely lenient, relying mostly on social admonition rather than capital punishment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Kautilya describes 'Dharmasthiya' for civil disputes and 'Kantakasodhana' for suppressing social thorns (crimes and state offenses). Statement 2 is incorrect because penal laws under the Mauryas were extremely harsh and rigorous, featuring capital punishment for numerous offenses to maintain strict imperial order.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Chandragupta Maurya's religious inclinations and death:
1. According to Jain traditions, he abdicated his throne in favor of his son Bindusara and embraced Jainism under Bhadrabahu.
2. He spent his final days at Ujjain performing ritual penance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Jain texts record that Chandragupta abdicated, followed Bhadrabahu, and went south. Statement 2 is incorrect because he spent his final days at Shravanabelagola in Karnataka, not Ujjain, where he performed Sallekhana.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the economic measures during Chandragupta Maurya's rule:
1. The state exercised strict monopolies over mining, salt extraction, and forest produce.
2. Currency circulation was expanded through punch-marked silver and copper coins issued by the imperial authority.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Arthashastra emphasizes state control over key economic sectors like mines and salt to generate massive revenue, and punch-marked coins became widespread during the Mauryan period to facilitate a unified imperial market.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the military and intelligence apparatus of Chandragupta Maurya:
1. The army was managed by a war office consisting of 30 members divided into six boards, each looking after infantry, cavalry, elephants, chariots, navy, and transport.
2. Intelligence gathering was restricted exclusively to foreign borders, with no domestic surveillance allowed on citizens.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Megasthenes notes the existence of a 30-member war council with six specialized boards. Statement 2 is incorrect because domestic surveillance was intense; Gudhapurushas (secret agents) extensively monitored citizens, ministers, and officials to preempt treason and dissent.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the territorial reach and unification achieved by Chandragupta Maurya:
1. His empire successfully brought the entire southern peninsula up to Kanyakumari under direct centralized administration.
2. He laid the foundation for the first pan-Indian empire by unifying northern, eastern, western, and northwestern regions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because direct Mauryan administration under Chandragupta did not extend to the far south (Tamilakam was beyond direct control, though later Ashoka's inscriptions mention southern neighbors). Statement 2 is correct, as he unified the major parts of northern, central, eastern, and northwestern India into a cohesive empire.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the matrimonial and diplomatic alliances of Chandragupta Maurya:
1. Chandragupta entered into a matrimonial alliance with Seleucus Nicator, marrying the Greek general's daughter.
2. The alliance resulted in Greece obtaining permanent suzerainty over the Mauryan capital of Pataliputra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: historical accounts note a matrimonial alliance following the 303 BCE treaty. Statement 2 is entirely incorrect; Seleucus was defeated and ceded territories to Chandragupta, meaning the Mauryas held absolute sovereignty, and Megasthenes came to Pataliputra as an ambassador, not a conqueror.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the governance and public works under Chandragupta Maurya:
1. Irrigation and water management were considered important state responsibilities, as evidenced by early references to dam and reservoir construction.
2. The central government completely ignored local village panchayats and tribal councils, imposing autocratic governors everywhere.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: irrigation works (such as the Sudarshana lake in Gujarat, whose construction began under Chandragupta's provincial governor Pushyagupta) were heavily supported by the state. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Mauryan administration coexisted with local autonomous bodies, village headmen (Gramika), and customary laws.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the historical identification of Chandragupta Maurya by European scholars:
1. Sir William Jones successfully identified 'Sandrokottos' mentioned in Greek texts with Chandragupta Maurya.
2. This chronological identification anchored ancient Indian chronology to Alexander the Great's invasion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Sir William Jones matched the Greek name 'Sandrokottos' with Chandragupta, which provided a crucial anchor date (tying Indian history to the precise chronology of Alexander's campaigns in 326 BCE) for reconstructing ancient Indian history.
